title: Equivalence between the Axion Invariant and the $S_4$ Symmetry Indicator
abstract: The equivalence between the axion invariant and the $S_4$ symmetry indicator is established for three-dimensional $S_4$-symmetric axion insulators with vanishing three-dimensional Chern numbers. Starting from the Chern-Simons expression for the magnetoelectric polarizability, $2P_3=θ/π$ is rewritten in terms of the $S_4$ sewing matrix. After stable reduction to determinant-one two-band blocks, the invariant is expressed as the degree of a map from the Brillouin zone to $SU(2)$. The degree modulo two is then evaluated from the $S_4$ eigenvalues at the four $S_4$-invariant momenta and is shown to coincide with the symmetry indicator $z_2$. A minimal tight-binding model verifies the correspondence between $2P_3$ and $z_2$. The result closes a gap between the topological-field-theory description of the axion response and the topological-band-theory classification by symmetry indicators. It also extends the known response-indicator equivalence from antiunitary settings such as $C_nT$ symmetry to the unitary, orientation-reversing rotoinversion symmetry $S_4$.
summary: This paper establishes a rigorous mathematical equivalence between the quantized magnetoelectric response (the axion invariant $2P_3$) and the symmetry indicator ($z_2$) for a specific class of topological insulators possessing $S_4$ symmetry. By connecting these two seemingly different theoretical frameworks, it provides a powerful new tool to classify and predict topological properties in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The paper establishes a mathematical equivalence between two distinct topological invariants characterizing axion insulators: the Chern-Simons derived magnetoelectric polarizability ($2P_3$) and a symmetry indicator ($z_2$). This bridges concepts from topological field theory (response) and band theory (symmetry classification).
main_result: The authors prove that for $S_4$-symmetric axion insulators with zero Chern numbers, the quantized magnetoelectric response $2P_3$ is exactly equal to the symmetry indicator $z_2$. This extends known equivalences to unitary, orientation-reversing symmetries.
method: The analysis involves rewriting the Chern-Simons expression using an $S_4$ sewing matrix, reducing the problem to calculating the degree of a map from the Brillouin zone to SU(2), and comparing this result with the calculation of $z_2$ based on eigenvalues at high-symmetry momenta.
model_or_system: The study focuses on three-dimensional axion insulators possessing $S_4$ symmetry. A specific tight-binding Hamiltonian is introduced for verification, allowing numerical confirmation of the theoretical equivalence.
key_observables: Axion invariant ($2P_3$), Symmetry Indicator ($z_2$), and the $S_4$ sewing matrix eigenvalues at high-symmetry points.
important_parameters: The symmetry group $S_4$, vanishing three-dimensional Chern numbers, and the modulo two arithmetic used in degree calculations.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on stable reduction to determinant-one two-band blocks and assumes that the system has vanishing three-dimensional Chern numbers.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates mapping degrees between circles; Figure 2 shows the band structure of the model; and Figure 3 displays the Density of States (DOS) for the model, with captions detailing specific matrix values at high-symmetry points.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the problem using the Chern-Simons form, then mathematically transforming this into a degree calculation involving the $S_4$ sewing matrix. It details the reduction to two-band blocks and finally proves the equivalence with the symmetry indicator via eigenvalue counting and numerical verification.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for theoretical physicists studying topological phases of matter, particularly those bridging continuum field theory descriptions (like axion electrodynamics) with discrete band structure calculations using crystalline symmetries.
